result:
Post revisions are implemented and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app or exercise the routes over HTTP, so the behaviour is checked by reading the code, not by running it.

Every successful edit now keeps the post's previous title, excerpt and body as a row in `post_revisions`, and deleting a post removes its revisions. The new history page is at `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.tsx`, with a Revisions link added to the post page for the author. Restoring is a `POST` route in `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts` that keeps the current version as a revision before writing the chosen one back. Both routes redirect guests to `/login` and return 403 for non-authors and 404 for a revision that belongs to another post. The table is defined in `db/schema.ts`, and the migration `db/migrations/20261018221844_previous_morbius.sql` was generated with `void db generate`. The shared helpers live in `lib/revisions.ts`, and the save and restore writes are batched so the revision and the post update succeed or fail together. The migration still needs to be applied to the database (for example with `void db migrate` or on deploy) before the routes will work.
